title: Medivnyk
subtitle: Ukrainian honey spice cake
excerpt: Medivnyk is a traditional Ukrainian honey cake made with dark flower honey, spices, and eggs, producing a dense, moist cake that keeps and improves over several days. It is associated with Christmas and Easter in Ukraine and the diaspora, eaten as part of the celebratory sweet table. The spice profile is warm rather than sharp, cinnamon, cloves, and ginger, and the honey gives it a slightly sticky crumb that holds together cleanly when sliced.
sourceNotes: Medivnyk (Ukrainian: медівник, meaning honey cake) is one of the most traditional Ukrainian baked goods and appears in recipes dating back several centuries. It is part of a broader family of Eastern European honey cakes, similar to Polish miodownik, Russian pryaniki (spiced honey biscuits), and German Lebkuchen, all of which reflect the historical importance of beekeeping in the region. The Ukrainian version is distinguished by its simple construction as a layer or loaf cake rather than a rolled biscuit, its use of warm rather than anise-forward spices, and its association with religious and family celebrations. Recipes vary by region; this version follows the most common home-baking approach using bicarbonate of soda for rise rather than yeast.

recipe.freezeNotes: Wrap well and freeze for up to 3 months. Defrost at room temperature overnight.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Medivnyk is best eaten after 24 to 48 hours when the flavour and texture have settled. It keeps for up to 2 weeks wrapped at room temperature.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: conventional 170°C or fan 150°C; skewer in the centre comes out clean when done

content.text: Medivnyk is a dense honey spice cake that tastes better on the second day than the first. The honey gives it a moist, slightly sticky crumb; the warm spices, cinnamon, cloves, ginger, deepen as the cake rests. Use a dark, strongly flavoured honey (buckwheat is traditional; forest or heather honey is a good substitute). Mild acacia honey won't give enough depth.

Combine the honey, butter, and brown sugar in a medium saucepan over a low heat. Stir until the butter has melted and the sugar dissolved. Remove from the heat and leave to cool to room temperature, the eggs go in next and the mixture must not be hot enough to scramble them.

Preheat the oven to 170°C conventional (150°C fan). Grease and line a 20 cm round tin or 900 g loaf tin. Beat the eggs into the cooled honey mixture one at a time. Add the soured cream. In a separate bowl, combine the flour, bicarbonate of soda, and all the spices. Fold the dry ingredients into the wet until just combined. The batter will be thick and glossy.

Pour into the prepared tin and bake for 40 to 45 minutes until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean. The cake will be deep mahogany in colour. Cool in the tin for 20 minutes, then turn out. Wrap in baking parchment and leave for at least 24 hours before cutting, the flavour mellows and the crumb becomes denser and more cohesive overnight.
